Rows are the CODEX rows (settled.json powers, movementAction — published by the content chat 2026-08-21): power.move (1 Stam, universal to all units), power.sidestep (free, COOLDOWN 1 — her ruling the same day: "it's available every other turn"; granted to Warrior/Mage/Priest/Paladin), power.side-roll (1 Stam, no cooldown; Rogue/Ranger). Engine: MoveDef rows in content/moves.ts, ctx.moves registry, grants in unit data end-to-end (RAW rows + settled.json testCohort -> pack), executeMove takes the CHOSEN power (the MOVE_STAMINA_COST constant died), executeSidestep is the one-hex shape, cooldowns share the ability gate (Codex counts Turns DOWN: ready = turn+cd+1). spec: PLAYBACK-DESIGN §6.2, §11.3, §13 item 1. THE ONE ENGINE CHANGE THE PLAYBACK REBUILD NEEDS. A scenario names a fielding from outside and gets it into an export: `engine/src/content/scenarios/<id>.json`, explicit-array registry, plus `npx tsx tools/export-battle.mts --scenario <id>`. createBattle already accepts heroes/mapId/enemyCount/heroHexes/enemyHexes — every ingredient exists; what is missing is a way to NAME a fielding. Rationale, measured 2026-08-21: across 640 battles on all 8 maps at two army sizes, power.flight, power.flight-swift and power.flight-labored fired ZERO times, as did all four beast attacks — because the beasts are player units benched until party assembly exists. movement.flight landed having never once run in a real fight. CONSTRAINT, ruled: a scenario names units and positions and MUST NOT accept stat overrides. Overrides belong to sweeps; a showcase that can change numbers is a showcase that can lie about the game. Positions validate as passable at load, loudly (Law 9).
expect: a scenario id fields the named units at the named hexes and exports a battle whose log mentions ids no standard battle can produce (the benched beasts, the flight ladder); an out-of-range or impassable hex throws at scenario load rather than silently relocating
note: Gate 1: probe.mts runs createBattle over the standard MAP_PANEL and cannot field a scenario, so no standard battle can mention a scenario id. Expect `unreachable` with a written reason, which flags the landing for review — the correct outcome, not a dodge.

spec: PLAYBACK-DESIGN §7.2, §13 item 2. field-geometry.mts emits BOARD SPACE, unsquashed: colStep 128 · rowStep 96 · oddOffset 64 · cell 128x132, and BASE_Y is dropped. The board applies rotateX(49.3deg) once at layer 0 — 49.3 is ruled (the angle the whole mapgen asset pipeline was built at; the Muster mock's 46 is superseded). Today the constants are HEXW 68.2, HEXH 59.675, ROW 44.8, BASE_Y 30.2 — an art-traced FLAT projection with the foreshortening already baked into the row step, which cannot be re-tilted without re-deriving every constant. Verified 2026-08-21: field-geometry.mts has exactly ONE consumer, tools/build-replay.mjs, and test/replay.test.ts does not read its constants at all — so unlike scenario.export this needs no cross-thread coordination and can land on its own.
expect: a 12x12 board measures 1600 x 1188 board px and presents 1600 x 826 after tilt; cos(49.3) = 0.6521, so a 96px row step lands at 62.6px and a 132px hex face at 86.1px

spec: PLAYBACK-DESIGN §7.1, §7.2, §7.2a, §7.4, §7.4a, §13 item 5. The Muster stage: layer stack in paint order, geometry consumed in board space with one rotateX(49.3deg) at layer 0, per-hex battle-scale swatches as the ground plane, the token presence stack (faction ring, contact shadow, selection ring, billboard, status glyphs with corner pips, HP and protection bars, move chip). spec: PLAYBACK-DESIGN §7.3, §7.3a, §7.3b, §13 item 6. THE BIGGEST GAP in the effect stack: nothing today draws PERSISTENT ground state. hexVFX plays events; a burning hex must still be burning next Turn. One node per affected hex against the TileState shape, fed from terrain at map.loaded so that when the engine gains dynamic ground events (gap L-2) only the feed changes. Governing rules: terrain keeps >=60% contribution and layers differ by HUE never by alpha — with darkness the one deliberate exception, ruled fully black because concealment IS the mechanic. Patch edges are a soft falloff; a hard-clipped hex is still a bug.
expect: burning, frost, poisoned and darkness persist across Turns on the hexes their terrain names, each owning a different channel, and no layer hides the terrain beneath it except darkness
note: Fog is NOT part of this item — it is blocked on engine vision (gap L-3) and is structurally distinct: unbounded, above the units, hides them.

spec: PLAYBACK-DESIGN §7.6, §7.6a, §6.4, §13 item 7. The Muster panel, faction-accented, 472px. Order: identity, HP/Protection, six-cell stat grid, status chips, card art, STAMINA, abilities — stamina sits between the art and the ability list because it pays for them. RULED: the panel is about WHOEVER IS ACTING, not click-driven; subject resolves inspect > target > acting, and the panel states which of the three it is doing. Ability rows are defined boxes, not table rows, carrying a class rule and four bordered cells RNG/DMG/AP/CD. Consequence: enemies need real card art, because an enemy activation puts an enemy in the panel every Enemy Phase — 147 painted enemy cards already exist in assets/bestiary/.
expect: the panel follows the acting unit without a click, swaps to the target during resolution, labels which mode it is in, and the fired ability row flashes on the beat
note: The six-cell stat grid shows STATIC values — gap L-1: unit.enter carries no armor/resist/dodge/accuracy/reach/movement and no event reports a change to them.

spec: PLAYBACK-DESIGN §4, §8, §13 item 8. The event pump against the full §4 mapping and the DUR table of §8. Every event either has a beat or is explicitly silent-but-logged; there is no third category. THE SPLIT SWING is the hard part and the reason the naive one-event-one-beat mapping is wrong: a projectile takes ~700ms, so the travel half plays on attack.declared/attack.hit and the impact half is HELD until damage.applied — otherwise the bolt lands on a target that already took the damage. attack.hit is DUR 0 on purpose: its beat is a Promise that resolves when the projectile lands, and the pump awaits that, not a number. The speed multiplier scales durations uniformly and must never scale ORDER — at x4 the split swing must still split.
expect: all 37 event types are handled, damage never lands before its projectile at any speed multiplier, and an unknown event type logs a finding line and continues rather than stopping an otherwise honest replay
note: The event contract is 37 rows, not the 36 the first draft of §3.2 listed — battle.end was omitted. On the wire its only field beyond the envelope is `outcome`; `turn` is already an envelope field.

spec: PLAYBACK-DESIGN §7.7, §13 item 9. The log is built UP FRONT, one sentence per event, before playback starts — so it greps without playing and a reviewer can read a battle without watching it; playback only marks the current line. Three filterable channels: main, debug (trigger.rolled, ai.mode), findings. Scroll the log box, never the page — scrollIntoView walks up every scrollable ancestor including <html>, so the board drifts off screen during playback, visible only when watching and never in a test. THE ACTIVATION STRIP IS NOT AN INITIATIVE RAIL: the engine has no initiative, but this is playback and the recorded activation.begin order IS the order. Sentence voice agrees with src/view/text.ts; where they diverge, text.ts is right.
expect: the full log exists in the DOM before play is pressed, the board never drifts during playback, and the activation strip shows recorded order without predicting anything

spec: PLAYBACK-DESIGN §4.4, §13 item 10. Three hexVFX styles are OWED and currently borrow another: status.stun borrows shadow, status.slow borrows frost, status.protection borrows weak. Author them natively in VFX/hexVFX.js, the canonical and only copy. One hue per status everywhere — pips, board glyphs, panel chips and hexVFX all read the single table. status.regeneration keeps its square pip: a shape cue on top of hue so the one helpful status can never be misread as poison. blight and shadow have no content behind them and may be re-pointed at poisoned ground and darkness; affliction is otherwise dead.
expect: stun, slow and protection each play a native style, and no status silently falls back to poison-green — the fallback is the exact legibility bug that was caught by eye
